::: {.callout-note title="Work in progress"}
This is a curriculum implementation plan. Completed lessons are linked as they become classroom-ready; later sections show the intended learning sequence.
:::

The track extends regular TEJ work with mathematics and modelling used in first-year engineering. It is useful for students interested in electrical, computer, mechatronics, mechanical, systems, or chemical engineering.

## Circuit sequence

1. [Engineering calculations](#engineering-calculations)
2. [Ohm's law and power](#ohms-law-and-power)
3. [Series circuits](#series-circuits)
4. [Parallel circuits](#parallel-circuits)
5. [Series-parallel circuits](#series-parallel-circuits)
6. [Kirchhoff's laws](#kirchhoffs-laws)
7. [Linear algebra for circuits](#linear-algebra-for-circuits)
8. [Equivalent circuits and optimization](#equivalent-circuits-and-optimization)
9. [Material and energy balances](#material-and-energy-balances)
10. [Transient systems](#transient-systems)
11. [Sensors and measurement](#sensors-and-measurement)

## Engineering calculations

**I will be able to** use units, metric prefixes, engineering notation, significant figures, ratios, estimation, and the GUESS method.

**This is useful because I can** catch mistakes and communicate a calculation clearly.

**Used in university:** Every engineering course expects correct units, notation, and documented calculations. [[1, Chs. 0–1]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Ohm's law and power

**I will be able to** calculate voltage, current, resistance, power, and safe component limits.

**This is useful because I can** predict whether a basic circuit will work safely before I build it.

**Used in university:** Circuit analysis, electronics laboratories, design courses, and energy calculations. [[1, Chs. 1, 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Series circuits

**I will be able to** calculate total resistance, circuit current, voltage drops, and power in a one-path circuit.

**This is useful because I can** predict and check every value in a complete series circuit.

**Used in university:** Direct-current circuit analysis and introductory electrical laboratories. [[1, Ch. 4]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

[Open the Series Circuits lesson package](../electronics-library/modules/h09-series-circuits-a.qmd)

## Parallel circuits

**I will be able to** calculate equivalent resistance, source current, branch currents, and branch power in a parallel circuit.

**This is useful because I can** explain how several loads operate from the same source voltage.

**Used in university:** Network analysis, electrical distribution, instrumentation, and electronics. [[1, Ch. 5]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Series-parallel circuits

**I will be able to** identify series and parallel groups, redraw a circuit, reduce it step by step, and work back to each branch value.

**This is useful because I can** turn a mixed circuit into smaller problems and prove the final answer.

**Used in university:** Network reduction, circuit laboratories, and preparation for Kirchhoff analysis. [[1, Ch. 6]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

[Open the Series-Parallel Circuits lesson package](../electronics-library/modules/h11-series-parallel-circuits-a.qmd)

## Kirchhoff's laws

**I will be able to** apply Kirchhoff's current law at a node and Kirchhoff's voltage law around a loop.

**This is useful because I can** write equations for circuits that cannot be reduced by inspection.

**Used in university:** Nodal analysis, mesh analysis, electronics, power systems, and control hardware. [[1, Ch. 9]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

::: {.callout-tip title="Recommended Grob sequence"}
Chapter 9 can follow Chapter 6. Students already have the series, parallel, and reduction skills needed for Kirchhoff analysis. Teach the relevant meter-safety material from Chapter 8 before physical measurements; Chapter 7 can be returned to later.
:::

## Linear algebra for circuits

**I will be able to** turn node and loop equations into a two- or three-variable system and solve it by elimination, substitution, matrices, and software.

**This is useful because I can** solve several unknown currents or voltages at the same time.

**Used in university:** Linear algebra, numerical methods, statics, structures, circuits, process models, and control. [[28, Chs. 9, 12]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

## Equivalent circuits and optimization

**I will be able to** use dividers, Thévenin and Norton equivalents, maximum power transfer, constraints, and sensitivity.

**This is useful because I can** replace a complicated source network with a simpler model and compare designs.

**Used in university:** Circuit design, modelling, optimization, and instrumentation. [[1, Chs. 7, 10]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Material and energy balances

**I will be able to** define a system boundary and calculate input, output, accumulation, loss, and efficiency.

**This is useful because I can** show where material or energy goes and explain what is lost.

**Used in university:** Chemical, mechanical, environmental, and energy engineering. [[27, Chs. 3, 5–6]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008)

## Transient systems

**I will be able to** model resistor-capacitor charging, signal smoothing, and heating or cooling with time constants and numerical steps.

**This is useful because I can** predict how a real system changes over time instead of assuming it responds instantly.

**Used in university:** Differential equations, circuits, heat transfer, process dynamics, and control. [[1, Ch. 22]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Sensors and measurement

**I will be able to** select and calibrate sensors and report range, sensitivity, resolution, accuracy, repeatability, error, and uncertainty.

**This is useful because I can** decide whether measured data is trustworthy.

**Used in university:** Engineering laboratories, instrumentation, experiments, robotics, and process control. [[1, Ch. 8]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Curve fitting, regression, and machine learning

**I will be able to** fit a model to sensor data, inspect residuals, separate training and test data, and compare prediction error with a baseline.

**This is useful because I can** find a useful pattern without assuming the first model is correct.

**Used in university:** Data analysis, numerical methods, system identification, experiments, and introductory machine learning. [[28, Chs. 17, 20]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010)

## Motors and electromechanical systems

**I will be able to** calculate force, torque, speed, electrical input power, mechanical output power, efficiency, and operating limits.

**This is useful because I can** connect circuit behaviour to useful motion.

**Used in university:** Mechanical, electrical, mechatronics, robotics, and systems engineering. [[1, Chs. 13–14]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Boolean logic, algorithms, and state machines

**I will be able to** use logic gates, truth tables, Boolean expressions, algorithms, state diagrams, and test cases.

**This is useful because I can** turn clear rules into a system that can be tested.

**Used in university:** Digital logic, programming, computer architecture, embedded systems, and control.

## Sensor, logic, and actuator project

**I will be able to** combine sensor thresholds, Boolean logic, and a protected driver circuit to control a motor, fan, relay, alarm, or indicator.

**This is useful because I can** build a complete system that senses, decides, and acts safely.

**Used in university:** Mechatronics, embedded systems, robotics, automation, and design projects.

## Number systems and digital representation

**I will be able to** use binary, decimal, hexadecimal, signed and unsigned integers, two's complement, fixed-point, floating-point, range, resolution, and overflow.

**This is useful because I can** choose how a computer stores a value and predict what can go wrong.

**Used in university:** Programming, computer engineering, embedded systems, numerical methods, and digital signal processing.

## Operational amplifiers and calculus

**I will be able to** analyze ideal operational-amplifier circuits and connect integrator and differentiator circuits to slope, area, and rate of change.

**This is useful because I can** see calculus operate on a real voltage signal.

**Used in university:** Calculus, analog electronics, instrumentation, signals, and control. [[1, Ch. 33]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)

## Feedback and control

**I will be able to** compare open-loop, on-off, hysteresis, proportional, integral, and derivative control using response, error, stability, and saturation.

**This is useful because I can** make a system correct itself and explain why poor settings cause problems.

**Used in university:** Control systems, robotics, mechatronics, chemical processes, and automation.

## Engineering design project

**I will be able to** define requirements, model a system, create a schematic and program, select sensors and actuators, build or simulate, test, validate, and revise.

**This is useful because I can** combine the track into one working, evidence-based design.

**Used in university:** Design courses, laboratories, capstone projects, and technical communication.

## Core references

The textbooks guide the sequence and level. Student materials use original explanations, diagrams, values, and questions.

[[1]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) **Grob's Basic Electronics, 12th edition** — direct-current circuits, measurement, network analysis, transients, and operational amplifiers.

[[27]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) **Çengel, Introduction to Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer, 2nd edition** — units, energy balances, efficiency, and transient thermal behaviour.

[[28]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) **Chapra and Canale, Numerical Methods for Engineers, 6th edition** — linear systems, modelling, regression, optimization, and numerical methods.
